text:
emma (support): Customer ACME reporting sudden p99 spike ~3x and intermittent 503s since 09:12 UTC. They say requests are hitting eu-west unexpectedly. attaching traces they captured.
acme-engineer: here's one trace, look at hop list: traceroute to api.redwood.ai (resolved to 52.50.11.23)
  1  10.0.0.1  1.2 ms
  2  198.51.100.2  10.3 ms
  3  52.50.11.23 (eu-west-1)  220.4 ms <-- unexpected
  4  * * *
Also saw a handful of 503s with X-Region: us-west but backend logged eu-west token mismatch.
emma (support): repro steps they used:
  1) curl -v -H "X-Request-ID: acme-123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  2) observed latency 230ms and trace header X-Trace: t-0a7b
  3) traceroute to resolved IP shows eu hop
raj (infra): pinging infra metrics now. any chance this is a customer-side DNS cache or CDN edge routing issue? :thinking:
marta (eng-sre): can you paste the full HTTP request/response headers around a failing request? especially X-Region, Forwarded, and any TLS SNI values.
acme-engineer: sample response headers from 09:15 UTC:
  HTTP/2 503 Service Unavailable
  date: Tue, 09 Mar 2026 09:15:42 GMT
  x-region: us-west-2
  x-fallback-region: eu-west-1
  x-request-id: acme-123
  content-type: application/json
  x-retry-after: 2
emma (support): they also ran `dig api.redwood.ai` and sometimes get US IPs, sometimes EU IPs - TTL looks normal (60s) but responses differ by resolver.
raj (infra): seeing a small spike in cross-region egress at 09:12. Noting route policy #42 had a transient route preference change due to an internal peering flapping event. Could explain EU path selection for some AS paths.
marta (eng-sre): two hypotheses:
  1) client resolve returned EU egress IP -> routed to eu region (normal).
  2) header-based region affinity got stripped by a customer proxy or intermediate -> our smart routing fell back to a compatible region (eu) and auth tokens mismatched causing 503s.
Let's triage with concrete repro: ask ACME to run curl with explicit host mapping to force US egress and include trace header.
  curl -v --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:18.197.10.50 \ 
    -H "X-Request-ID: acme-repro-1" \ 
    -H "X-Region-Hint: us-west-2" \ 
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
If this yields low latency and no 503s, it's resolver/peering. If still goes to eu, then path rewrite/proxy.
acme-engineer: running that now... holding.
deploy-bot: canary traffic routed through policy-42 at 09:11:45 UTC, small failover to backup peering triggered 09:12:03 UTC.
acme-engineer: repro result: when forcing 18.197.10.50 I get 42ms and no 503. default DNS gave EU IP and 230ms + occasional 503.
marta (eng-sre): that confirms DNS/peering path. action items:
  - raj, can infra confirm which upstream resolver returned EU IPs at 09:12 and whether our edge announced different anycast prefixes briefly?
  - support: ask ACME for their resolver (systemd-resolved? corporate appliance?) and TTL behavior. Also ask if they have any on-prem load balancer that rewrites X-Region-Hint.
raj (infra): checking BGP/peering logs and anycast registers. initial quick check: one peering session to IX-AMS had brief route withdrawal at 09:11:58 UTC -> some resolvers may have re-resolved and gotten eu-side IPs. I'll correlate with our edge anycast announcers.
emma (support): ACME says they use a managed DNS (internal corporate appliance) that does occasional geo-answers. they've escalated to their DNS provider.
marta (eng-sre): mitigation options:
  - add a stronger region affinity header that survives proxies (e.g., signed region hint) — medium effort.
  - add a temporary server-side rule: prefer last-successful-region cookie for a tenant, don't fall back across continents for 503s within 30s window — short-term mitigation.
  - inform sales/billing: because p99 spike was transient we should be careful about charge adjustments if ACME asks.
raj (infra): will follow up with peering ops and post back with timeline. I suspect route flap + resolver behavior explains the EU hop. also will flag policy-42 for a small tweak to prefer same-continent fallbacks.
acme-engineer: thanks, we're going to monitor. keeping this thread open if you need more traces.
emma (support): noted. I'll add repro commands and recommended mitigation to the customer ticket and mark high urgency. :thumbsup:
